tasks.short: Patrol parking areas to prevent vehicle damage and thefts.

steps.what: Patrol parking areas and watch vehicles and property
Decide if vehicle damage or property thefts are underway
Tell the driver or a colleague about the vehicle
Write the accepted note of vehicle damage or thefts
File the accepted note in the parking incident register
steps.handoff_to: First-Line Supervisors of Material-Moving Machine and Vehicle Operators

tasks.design: She still patrols the parking areas and still decides whether vehicle damage or a theft is underway, then tells the driver or a colleague in person. When she accepts an incident note, {OTHER} (the parking incident register) files that note once. The file step sends no message and places no call.
tasks.previous_blocker: The incident note sat in a pocket book until someone recopied it, so a colleague could not see the bay and the damage until the next handover.
tasks.enabler_now: A records register can store the fields she already types, with no model watching the lot.
tasks.still_hard: Telling an owner from a theft, and stopping damage, still happen while she is in the parking area.
tasks.human_edge: She can tell an owner from a theft while she is standing by the vehicle. A filed note does not make that call.

ambition.what: Record a damaged vehicle the same shift it is seen, instead of waiting for the next shift handover.

tasks.altitude: She still patrols the whole shift and still speaks to the driver or the colleague in person. The only change is that an accepted note is filed once.

reach.role: First-Line Supervisors of Material-Moving Machine and Vehicle Operators
reach.task: Follow up on vehicle damage found in the parking areas
reach.learn: Which vehicle her accepted note marks as damaged or at risk, and the bay she wrote.

evidence.claim: A records register can store the incident fields she typed in the note. It does not shorten the patrol, the decision, or the in-person talk. This is model knowledge.
A data-protection impact assessment is mandatory for systematic employee monitoring, location data and cameras on public space.
Works-council consent is needed for tachograph analysis and for control-room cameras that also watch staff.
Annex III point 2 of the EU AI Act covers safety components in road traffic management.

assumptions: Fields she types in s4, which produces the note s5 files: bay or row, what she saw (damage or theft), still at risk (yes or no), and the time of day. No staff name, no route, no camera image.
If the bay is unclear she types a short place description in s4. s5 has no other source.
s5 files only the note she accepted in s4. A later edit voids that approval. If she writes no note, s5 does not run.
Speaking to a driver or a colleague is a talk in the lot, not a send outside the organisation. s3 is not a gate and not act_external. s5 does not send a message and does not place a call.
Upkeep is about 1 hour per 100 baseline hours: bay names and a short list of damage phrases, a few times a year.
The register does not watch staff and does not track her location. It is not a traffic-management safety component.
unknowns: Whether the lot already keeps an incident book or only a spoken handover.
Whether a works council would treat a stored note as a check on how she patrols.
Whether the site expects a vehicle plate on the note. The design does not require one.
Whether insurance keeps a separate damage file she still fills by hand.
research_questions: Does today's handover already keep bay, what she saw, still at risk, and time as separate fields?
Does anyone besides the lot staff open the note the same shift?

already_counted.description: She re-reads the incident note in s4 before she accepts it.

incremental.description: A few times a year she updates bay names and the short damage phrases in the register.

approvals.approved_version: incident note she accepted in s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most patrols find nothing to write, so the file step saves nothing and the low is 0. When she accepts a note, filing that version once is the high, 1, under the net of 2. The walk, the decision and the talk stay as they are.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still walks the parking areas and still warns people in person. An accepted damage or theft note is filed once from the version she wrote.
reach: First-Line Supervisors of Material-Moving Machine and Vehicle Operators
skills_to_grow: Writing an incident note in fixed fields
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor can see a damaged vehicle the same shift she accepts the note, including the bay she wrote.
